definition: In historical psychology, imbecility referred to a general weakness of mind, especially a congenital form of mental impairment regarded as less severe than idiocy. It implied marked limitations in memory, reasoning, and independent mental activity that were seen as preventing ordinary daily responsibilities and requiring special education.
